stemMd:
Five runners, P, Q, R, S and T, finish a race. There are no ties.

- Q finishes ahead of R.
- R finishes ahead of T.
- S finishes immediately after P.
- T finishes neither first nor last.

Which of the following must be true?
explanationMd:
Combine the first two conditions into one order: Q ahead of R ahead of T. Two runners finish ahead of T, so T is at least third. T is not last, so T is third or fourth.

- **T fourth.** The remaining places are 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 5th. P and S need two consecutive places, which can only be 1st and 2nd or 2nd and 3rd. Either way, one of Q and R is pushed into 5th place, behind T, which breaks the order Q, R, T. This case fails.
- **T third.** Q and R must take 1st and 2nd, in that order, and P and S take 4th and 5th, with S immediately after P.

The only possible finishing order is Q, R, T, P, S. So P finishes fourth.

What to notice first: chain the "ahead of" conditions into a single line, then use it to limit where the last runner in the chain can go.

distractorRationale.e: Q must be ahead of both R and T, and T is third, so Q is first. Second place belongs to R.
distractorRationale.d: R must finish behind Q, so R can never be first.
distractorRationale.b: Third place is taken by T in the only valid order. S finishes fifth, immediately after P.
distractorRationale.a: T in fourth place forces P and S into two consecutive places among 1st to 3rd, which pushes Q or R behind T. T must be third.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Q>R>T with T not first/last forces T=3 or 4. T=4: Q,R and the P-S block cannot fit (position 5 isolated would need Q or R, contradiction). So T=3, Q1, R2, P4, S5. Only C (P fourth) holds.
